newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - AMS results slide, sells SAMES stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - AMS results slide, sells SAMES stake.

text.p: Microchip maker Austria Mikro Systeme (AMS) reported on Wednesday a giddy fall in parent earnings for 1996 and a swing into the red on a group basis due to crumbling sales at its three companies.
AMS took the market by surprise when it admitted it was unable to turn around its loss-making subsidiary SAMES and had reduced its stake in the company to 19 percent from 51.

The AMS group, which consists of the parent company and two subsidiaries, Thesys and SAMES, attributed its earnings retreat in all key areas to price erosion, over-capacity and stagnating demand in the global semiconductor market.
"The results were not in line with expectations and were characterised by distinctly declining sales of all three companies," AMS said in a statement.

On a group basis, AMS reported a pre-tax loss of 100.6 million schillings ($8.3 million) after a profit of 266.9 million in 1995, and a bruising 74 percent fall in net income to 52 million on a 4.9 percent fall in sales to 1.79 billion.

"Everyone had been expecting bad results, but they came in worse than we were expecting," said an analyst at a British brokerage. "The big shock was in the movement in inventory -- which went to a loss of 111 million schillings (from a profit of 85.6 million)".
Also worrying was the order backlog, which on December 31 stood at just 418.2 million schillings, down 60 percent on the year-ago period.
AMS said that its 51.25 percent owned Thesys and 19 percent owned SAMES were especially hit by the difficult market conditions as both were mainly active as foundry suppliers.

Thesys reported a net loss of 125.6 million schillings last year, and SAMES a net loss of 39.6 million schillings in the first nine months of 1996. Year-ago comparisons were not made available for the two companies that AMS bought in 1995.
AMS said the group was "prepared for solid growth in 1997", but first quarter results of the current year, announced on Wednesday, painted a somewhat gloomy picture.
Group sales slumped to 344.9 million schillings from 572.8 million in the year-ago period while the order backlog fell to 574.7 million from 869.9 million.

However, the market focused on an increase in the order entry to 499.4 million schillings from 405.3 million in the first quarter and the company's assertion of better prospects in 1997 due to an improvement in the semiconductor industry.
"The stock's also up on the reduction of its stake in SAMES. A lot more restructuring was needed there, so they've now got somebody else to do it," the analyst in London said.
AMS divested part its stake in SAMES to the South African state-owned Industrial Development Corporation. The deal was signed on Tuesday but was made effective from September 30, 1996

For the full year, the parent company saw net profit sag to 107.7 million schillings from 217.3 million in 1995 as sales tumbled 25 percent to 1.28 billion. The order backlog dropped to 300.2 million, down 45.2 percent on the year-ago period.
"The decline in sales was primarily caused by a delay in the realisation of new projects as well as by a reduction of sales of major customers," AMS said.
The stock market shrugged off the results, sending the share price up three percent to 1,107 schillings in an overall limp Vienna market.
"The losses had already been largely discounted," said one trader. "These 1996 results had been expected. The only unknown element was the slashed dividend."
AMS said it would cut its dividend for 1996 by two schillings to pay out 10 schillings. ($ = 12.08 Austrian Schillings)
